newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Wednesday on profit-taking by retail investors, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,388 yuan ($408) per tonne, losing 32 yuan. It opened at 3,390 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,395 and a low of 3,385.
May rose 57 yuan to 3,360, July fell 10 to 3,386, November 35 to 3,395 and the January 1998 contract two to 3,398.
Combined volume fell to 16,000 tonnes from 17,100 tonnes.
Soybeans opened higher but selling at high levels pushed most contracts down for most of the session, traders said.
"Profit-taking dominated today's trading on a lack of market-moving news," one trader said. "The market has no clear trend up and that should keep investors on the sidelines."
Analysts said they expected soybeans to consolidate around current levels in the short term.
